artworks.title: Heracles and the Cretan Bull (Olympia metope)
artworks.artist: Unknown (workshop of the Master of Olympia)
artworks.description: Marble metope from the Temple of Zeus at Olympia: Heracles grapples Poseidon's white bull — the seventh Labour — locking horns and neck as he prepares to bring the beast alive to Eurystheus. The original relief is in the Archaeological Museum of Olympia.

artworks.title: Heracles and the Cretan Bull (detail of the Labours of Hercules mosaic from Llíria)
artworks.description: A panel from the Roman Labours pavement found at Llíria (Edeta) and now in the Museo Arqueológico Nacional, Madrid: Heracles captures the Cretan Bull, the living prize of the seventh Labour before the beast's later mythic career in Crete.

artworks.title: Heracles and the Cretan Bull (drawing after a red-figure vase)
artworks.artist: Unknown draughtsman (after an Attic red-figure vase)
artworks.description: A BnF drawing after a red-figure vase: Heracles subdues the Cretan Bull in the formula vase-painters used for the seventh Labour — the same bull Poseidon sent to Minos and that later sires the Minotaur's line.

artworks.title: Heracles and the Cretan Bull (engraved reconstruction of the Olympia metope)
artworks.description: Blouet's 1831 engraved reconstruction of the Olympia Temple of Zeus metope, published after the early excavations — a scholarly image that fixed the Early Classical struggle with the Cretan Bull for nineteenth-century viewers.

popCulture.title: Cretan Bull
popCulture.description: The bull Poseidon sent to Minos endures as Heracles' seventh labour — captured alive, and later the sire of the Minotaur's mother's passion.
